options.text: Divide the interval from $0$ to $1$ into $5$ equal lengths and count $3$ of those lengths from $0$.
Mark a point near $1$ because the printed $5$ looks large on the page.
The number-line placement rule also requires changing $\dfrac{3}{5}$ into another kind of number first.
Place $\dfrac{3}{5}$ by comparing only how large $3$ looks next to $5$ as a unit fraction of a different whole.

stem:
Chirag places the fraction $\dfrac{3}{5}$ on a number line marked from $0$ to $1$. The diagram shows that number line.

Which plan places $\dfrac{3}{5}$ correctly?

teacher.key_rationale: To place 3/5, partition [0,1] into 5 equal parts and take 3 from 0. Size of the printed digit, converting the fraction first, or comparing numerators as unit fractions of another whole are wrong plans.
teacher.figure_note: Number line from 0 to 1 with five equal tick intervals; mark at 3/5 queried.
